historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (The Conquest of Egypt). Ibn Abd al-Hakam recounts the events of the first Egyptian campaign (639-640 AD) led by Amr ibn al-As. Ulwaan is mentioned as one of the major towns that surrendered to the Arab forces, and its governor, 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-'Aas, was ordered to collect the jizya tax from its inhabitants.

Al-Maqrizi, The History of the Prophets and Kings. Ulwaan is mentioned as a city that welcomed the Fatimid caliph Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah when he migrated from Yemen to Egypt in 973 AD. The city later rebelled against him, and was punished with destruction.
